Details and the full pass mix appear here. Click a dot to keep it.
Bars = share of this player's open-play passes in each of the nine pass types; the black tick = the average for his type. Dot size = value created (xT per 90, x100; passes by default, or carries, or both). The map is the same for every season of a position, so a player who changes style moves across it: use "Follow a player" to see the path. Click a dot to keep it: the Plays like list below it names the eight players with the closest mix, and the season each one matched in. Click a name to jump there.

What are the nine pass types, and how was this made?

Method. 4.5 million open-play passes (2013/14 to 8 Nov 2026) were clustered with k-means into nine types using where each pass starts, how far it goes toward goal and sideways, and whether it was lofted or a cross. Each player-season is then his share of passes in each type. Players are grouped within position with k-means on those shares, with a separate pass cutoff and number of groups for each position, chosen by split-half reliability, silhouette and stability checks. Types (4, 3 and 4 groups) are the stable level; styles (7, 5 and 6 groups) are finer but their borders wobble, so treat them as neighbourhoods on a continuum. Names are the author's reading of each group's most-used passes.

Plays like. For the selected player-season the page computes the Hellinger distance (Euclidean distance between the square roots of the nine shares) to every other player-season of every position, keeps each other player's closest season, and lists the eight nearest. The noise scale is the typical distance between a player's own two half-seasons, rescaled to two full seasons: matches closer than that cannot be told apart from sampling noise. At 500+ passes the player's own other half-season was the very nearest only about one time in eight (median rank about 14 of 3,300), so read the list as a shortlist.

Carrying. A carry is the ball moving with a player between two events, inferred from event data (no speed, space or pressure); a take-on is an attempt to beat an opponent. Per 90 minutes the page shows carries, progressive carries (10 m or more closer to goal), take-ons and carry xT, each with its percentile among players of the same position and season, plus a three-level carry tier (thirds of a composite of carries, progressive carries and take-ons within position) and a dribbler tag (top third of take-ons per carry). Carries do not make the k-means groups more stable (tested: stability unchanged), so the types and styles above use passes only. They do help to tell players apart, which is why they sit in the Plays like list. The tier is fuzzy: a player is in the same third on his odd and even matches about 70 to 80% of the time. Carry xT before 2024/25 uses a grid fitted on the same data.

Caveats. Types form a continuum, not islands (silhouette about 0.2). Position is the one a player most often started in. Pass xT (value created by completed passes) ignores carrying, defending and off-ball work; xT before 2024/25 uses a grid fitted on the same data, so compare within a season. The 2026/27 season is only 8 matches per team old: players with 200+ passes are shown (full seasons use a cutoff of 150 for defenders and 250 for midfielders and attackers), so groups may still move. Data: WhoScored event data.
